query: How does resolution time vary across category, priority, and assignment group?

per_column.name: assigned_technician
per_column.rationale: Individual technician identity is an associational variable that could relate to resolution time, but with many distinct high-cardinality names it forms fine-grained categories that are hard to compare cleanly; overlaps with existing assigned_to. Marginally useful but not well-separated segmentation.

per_column.name: primary_issue_domain
per_column.rationale: Well-separated interpretable categories (connectivity, email, database, etc.) that can be grouped and compared against resolution time; a strong EDA segmentation axis, though somewhat correlated with category.

per_column.name: incident_closure_status
per_column.rationale: Open/closed status largely restates the existing 'state' field and is intertwined with whether resolution_time is even defined; not an external explanatory variable for how long resolution takes.

per_column.name: issue_complexity_signal
per_column.rationale: Interpretable, well-separated buckets (infrastructure_systemic, application_focused, user_access, endpoint_device) that plausibly associate with resolution time and support meaningful segmentation.

per_column.name: issue_severity_signal
per_column.rationale: Severity levels (outage_complete, partial_access, performance_degradation) are interpretable categories strongly associable with resolution time; good EDA axis, partially overlapping with priority.

per_column.name: same_person_closure_flag
per_column.rationale: A clean binary flag (opener==closer) that can be compared against resolution time and reflects a workflow characteristic; interpretable segmentation with reasonable balance.

per_column.name: caller_frequency_indicator
per_column.rationale: Ordinal, well-separated caller-frequency bands offer an external behavioral dimension to segment resolution time by; interpretable and balanced.

judge.rationale: Most added columns are external, interpretable, well-separated categorical segmentations (issue domain, complexity, severity, caller frequency, same-person closure flag) that let a human explorer group and compare resolution_time along meaningful dimensions. Weaknesses: incident_closure_status essentially restates the existing state and conditions whether resolution_time exists, and assigned_technician is high-cardinality and duplicative of assigned_to. Some signals overlap with existing category/priority axes, but as a set they open genuine informative relationships around the focus, warranting a fairly strong but not top score.
